# Pi.js 2.3.0 - Quick Reference for LLMs

## Overview

Pi.js is a browser-only WebGL 2 library for retro-style graphics, bitmap text, sound, and input.
Use `import { $ } from "pijs-web"` for ES modules. Examples use `$` as the API binding.
IIFE bundles expose `pi` and, when it is not already defined, `$` as globals.

## Key Facts

- Version: 2.3.0
- Full bundles gamepad, keyboard, sound, pointer, and polygons. Their standalone plugins are for
  Lite only: loading one after Full throws `DUPLICATE_PLUGIN`. `sound-advanced` is in neither
  bundle; load it after Full, or after Lite and `sound`.
- Input commands are camelCase: `inKey`, `onKey`, `inMouse`, `onPress`, `inGamepad`.
- `polygon( points, fillColor )` draws a closed outline with optional nonzero-winding fill.
- Polygon points accept flat arrays, typed arrays, or `{ x, y }` arrays; replace them to edit vertices.
- Create a screen before calling screen-scoped commands.
- Coordinates start at the top-left and use logical screen pixels.
- Rendering is automatic and pixel-perfect.
- Most commands accept positional arguments or one options object.
- Index 0 in a palette is reserved for transparent black.

## Setup and Drawing

```javascript
const main = $.screen( "320x200" );
$.setColor( "white" );
$.line( 0, 0, 100, 100 );
$.rect( 20, 20, 80, 40, "red" );
$.circle( 160, 100, 30, "blue" );
$.print( "Hello, Pi.js!" );
```

Aspect strings use `x` for exact dimensions, `m` for integer-multiple scaling, and `e` for
extending the logical area to fill the container:

```javascript
$.screen( "640x480" );
$.screen( "320m200", "game-container" );
$.screen( { "aspect": "320e200", "container": "game-container" } );
```

## Images and Resources

Load resources before waiting for readiness. `loadImage()` returns the registered image name;
`getImage()` retrieves its browser image element.

```javascript
const playerName = $.loadImage( "player.png", "player" );

$.ready( function() {
	$.screen( "320x200" );
	$.drawImage( playerName, 160, 100, null, 0.5, 0.5, 2, 2, 45 );
	const playerElement = $.getImage( playerName );
	console.log( playerElement.width, playerElement.height );
} );
```

`drawImage()` arguments after `x` and `y` are `color`, `anchorX`, `anchorY`, `scaleX`, `scaleY`,
and `angle` in degrees. Use `createImageFromScreen()` to capture framebuffer pixels.

```javascript
const captureName = $.createImageFromScreen( "capture", 0, 0, 63, 63 );
$.drawImage( captureName, 100, 20 );
$.removeImage( captureName );
```

Queued draws finish before `removeImage()` releases textures. Later draws using the removed name
throw `IMAGE_NOT_FOUND`.

## Colors and Settings

```javascript
$.setPal( [ "black", "white", "red", "green", "blue" ] );
$.setPalColors( [ 2, 3 ], [ "orange", "lime" ] );
const orangeIndex = $.getPalIndex( "orange", 0 );
const orange = $.getPalColor( orangeIndex );

$.set( {
	"color": orange,
	"blend": "alpha",
	"bgColor": "#101020"
} );
```

Supported blend modes are `"replace"` and `"alpha"`. Palette changes affect future drawing; they
do not recolor pixels already in the framebuffer.

## Views and Input

Views create nested local coordinate systems and clipping regions. Inside a view, `width()` and
`height()` return the requested view dimensions. Pointer coordinates remain screen-relative.

```javascript
$.screen( "320x200" );
$.pushView( 20, 20, 120, 80 );
$.cls();

// inMouse() is null until the first mouse event
const mouse = $.inMouse();
if( mouse && ( mouse.buttons & 1 ) ) {
	const localMouse = $.screenToView( mouse.x, mouse.y );
	$.circle( localMouse.x, localMouse.y, 3, "white" );
}

$.popView();
$.resetView();
```

The first read or handler registration starts tracking. Name keys by code, such as `"KeyA"`
or `"Space"`, for game controls:

```javascript
if( $.inKey( "ArrowLeft" ) ) {
	playerX -= 1;
}

function jump( keyData ) {
	console.log( keyData.code );
}
$.onKey( "Space", "down", jump );
$.offKey( "Space", "down", jump );
```

A handler is identified by its mode and function, so registering it twice runs it once, and
`offX( mode, fn )` removes it. Handlers run after state updates; one that throws is reported
with `console.error()`. Releases caused by blur, a hidden page, or a stop command reach `"up"`
handlers with `cancelled: true`.

Mouse, touch, press, and click data share one frozen shape: `x`, `y`, `lastX`, `lastY`,
`buttons`, `action`, `type`, `id`, and `cancelled`. Pointer modes are `"down"`, `"move"`, and
`"up"`. Touch handlers receive an array with the one touch that changed. `inMouse()` and
`inPress()` return `null` before the first event.

```javascript
$.onPress( "down", function( press ) {
	$.setColor( "yellow" );
	$.pset( press.x, press.y );
} );
$.onWheel( function( wheel ) {
	zoom += wheel.deltaY * 0.001;
} );
```

Gamepads are live objects updated in place; read them once per frame:

```javascript
const pad = $.inGamepad( 0 );
if( pad && pad.getButtonJustPressed( "south" ) ) {
	jump();
}
const x = pad ? pad.getAxis( "leftX" ) : 0;
```

`inGamepad()` without an index always returns an array. Button names follow the standard
mapping: `south`, `east`, `west`, `north`, shoulders, triggers, `dpadUp`, and so on; axes are
`leftX`, `leftY`, `rightX`, and `rightY`.

## Sound

Sound needs a page served over HTTP(S) and plays after the first user gesture.
One-shot sounds requested while audio is locked do not play. Looping audio and songs wait for
unlocking; sounds requested inside the unlocking gesture handler can play immediately.

```javascript
$.sound( 440, 0.2, 0.5, "square" );
$.sound( {
	"frequency": 220, "frequencyEnd": 880, "duration": 0.3,
	"attackTime": 0.01, "releaseTime": 0.2
} );
const song = $.play( "T140 L8 O4 C E G >C" );
$.stopPlay( song );

$.loadAudio( "music.ogg", "music", true );
await $.ready();
const instance = $.playAudio( "music", 0.6, 0, 0, true );
$.pauseAudio( instance );
$.resumeAudio( instance );
$.setBusVolume( "audio", 0.5 );
```

`sound()` positions are `frequency`, `duration`, `volume`, `oType`, `delay`, `attackTime`,
`decayTime`, `sustainLevel`, `releaseTime`, `pan`, and `frequencyEnd`. `playAudio()` returns an
instance ID for `stopAudio`, `pauseAudio`, `resumeAudio`, and `setAudio`. Sound, music, and
audio share 64 voices and mix on the `"sfx"`, `"music"`, and `"audio"` buses into the master
volume and an output limiter.

## Shaders

GPU framebuffers, image samplers, and custom shader outputs use **premultiplied RGBA**: RGB
is multiplied by alpha. Keep RGB between zero and alpha, and use zero RGB when alpha is zero.
Multiply all four channels to change opacity. To perform straight-color math, divide RGB by
alpha only when alpha is nonzero, then multiply the resulting RGB by the output alpha.

JavaScript colors, pixel read results, palette matching, filter callbacks, and captured canvas
images use straight RGBA. Readback returns zero RGB for fully transparent pixels; low-alpha
RGB is quantized by the internal RGBA8 storage.

`applyShader()` inserts a pass into framebuffer draw order. A display shader changes final
presentation without modifying the logical framebuffer.

```javascript
const invert = $.createShader( `#version 300 es
precision mediump float;
in vec2 v_texCoord;
uniform sampler2D u_texture;
out vec4 fragColor;

void main() {
	vec4 color = texture( u_texture, v_texCoord );
	fragColor = vec4( color.a - color.rgb, color.a );
}` );

$.screen( "320x200" );
$.circle( 160, 100, 40, "red" );
$.applyShader( invert );
console.log( $.getShaderInfo( invert ) );
$.removeShader( invert );
```

Shader source must use GLSL ES 3.00 and declare `uniform sampler2D u_texture`. Known uniforms with
invalid values throw synchronously.

## Pixels and Filters

`get( x, y, width, height )` returns palette-index rows; use `asIndex: false` for `PiColor` objects.
`getPixel()` returns a `PiColor` by default. `put()` takes index rows and skips index 0 unless
`include0` is true. Async reads reject with `SCREEN_REMOVED` if their screen is removed.
`filterImg()` defers a CPU filter. Its callback receives a reusable `Uint8ClampedArray` of
`[ r, g, b, a ]` plus view-local coordinates. Return truthy to keep the modified pixel, or falsy
to make it transparent. It reads pixels after synchronous drawing finishes, so capture its result
or draw above it on a later task or animation frame.

```javascript
$.filterImg( function( pixel ) {
	pixel[ 0 ] = 255 - pixel[ 0 ];
	pixel[ 1 ] = 255 - pixel[ 1 ];
	pixel[ 2 ] = 255 - pixel[ 2 ];
	return true;
} );
```

Context loss suspends screens sharing the context and discards drawing; reads return transparent
pixels and queued filters are canceled. Restoration rebuilds GPU resources with transparent
framebuffers. Settings and shader handles survive; redraw framebuffer content and GPU-only glyph
edits. A failed rebuild leaves rendering suspended and reports `WEBGL_CONTEXT_RESTORE_FAILED`.

## Parented Offscreen Screens

```javascript
const main = $.screen( "320x200" );
const layer = $.screen( {
	"aspect": "160x100",
	"isOffscreen": true,
	"parent": main
} );

layer.circle( 80, 50, 30, "red" );
main.drawImage( layer, 80, 50 );

layer.removeScreen();
main.removeScreen();
```

The parent shares its WebGL context but does not own the child. Remove both screens explicitly.

## Ready and Game Loops

```javascript
await $.ready();
$.screen( "320x200" );

function gameLoop() {
	$.cls();
	updateGame();
	drawGame();
	requestAnimationFrame( gameLoop );
}

gameLoop();
```

## Screen Layout and Resource Behavior

With `noCss: true` (default false), Pi.js leaves automatic canvas, container, html, and body
styles to host CSS. Supply usable canvas layout. Pi.js appends the canvas and manages its intrinsic
size and WebGL resources. Explicit background commands still apply their requested styles.
The `x` and `m` modes keep their requested logical dimensions; `e` computes its logical extent
from the container. With a display shader, backing size follows the canvas CSS content size before
transforms. Canvas and container changes are observed. Hidden hosts keep their last valid allocation
and recover when visible. Offscreen screens accept `noCss` as a no-op.

Pointer input requires an onscreen target. Creating an offscreen screen makes it active; use
`visible.inMouse()` or `$.setScreen( visible )` to read from the visible screen afterward.

Shader `v_texCoord` uses bottom-left/y-up UVs. Custom `sampler2D` sources have the same
orientation as `u_texture`. Drawing coordinates are top-left/y-down; convert UVs to logical pixels
with `vec2( uv.x, 1.0 - uv.y ) * u_sourceSize`. Direct video sources upload when resolved for
drawing or shader use and a decoded frame is available. First use without a decoded frame throws
`IMAGE_NOT_READY`; subsequent unavailable frames keep the last valid upload. Pi.js creates no
video rendering loop; request drawing or shader presentation as frames change.

Image `onLoad`/`onError` exceptions remain visible and release the resource wait exactly once.
`ready()` waits for resources to settle, including failures; it does not guarantee successful loads.
Failed screen creation rolls back its DOM, observers, commands, and GPU resources.
